label: TMUA 2020 · Paper 2 · Question 3

hints.title: Expand each line yourself
hints.body: Read the equalities from the beginning. When clearing the inner denominators, keep brackets around each entire numerator before subtracting.
hints.recap: A minus before a bracket changes every sign inside it.
hints.pitfall: A later line may follow correctly from an earlier incorrect line.
hints.pause: Compare your expansion with each displayed line and locate the first difference.

recall.reminder: Check each step using only the assumptions and earlier correct lines.

solution:
Line I is valid because 4=2×2. In line II, however, the inner multiplication should produce (9n+1)−(3n−1)=9n+1−3n+1=6n+2.

The student instead writes 9n+1−3n−1, failing to change the sign of the −1 inside the subtracted numerator. This is the first error.

The original expression actually equals 2(6n+2)=12n+4, rather than 12n. Line II is first wrong: C.
knowledgePattern: Locate the first invalid distribution of a minus sign
